items.readable_text:
Content:
In this lesson, we'll discuss some fundamental objects in geometry. The objects we'll discuss are some of the building blocks we use to describe all geometrical objects.

Content:
A point is an exact location in space. It has no size (i.e., no length, width, or depth), only position. A point is indicated with a dot usually labeled with a capital letter (e.g., [MATH: P], [MATH: Q], [MATH: S], ...), as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/394131851a697a92fe0820c40e84d994]

Content:
A line is a straight object that is infinitely long and has no width. We can think of it as an infinite collection of points, extending infinitely in both directions. A line has no endpoints!

Content:
Let's take a look at the following line.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cefde0211d0bfe21ca3234a1a5ec81d0]

Content:
A line that passes through the points [MATH: P] and [MATH: Q] is expressed as
[MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PQ}.]

Content:
We use the "[MATH: \longleftrightarrow]" symbol to denote that the line extends forever in both directions.

Content:
Lines can also be indicated with lowercase letters. For example:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/ea3401bcfecd7809c0a16876239a27f9]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
In this lesson, we'll discuss some fundamental objects in geometry. The objects we'll discuss are some of the building blocks we use to describe all geometrical objects.

Content:
A point is an exact location in space. It has no size (i.e., no length, width, or depth), only position. A point is indicated with a dot usually labeled with a capital letter (e.g., [MATH: P], [MATH: Q], [MATH: S], ...), as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/394131851a697a92fe0820c40e84d994]

Content:
A line is a straight object that is infinitely long and has no width. We can think of it as an infinite collection of points, extending infinitely in both directions. A line has no endpoints!

Content:
Let's take a look at the following line.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cefde0211d0bfe21ca3234a1a5ec81d0]

Content:
A line that passes through the points [MATH: P] and [MATH: Q] is expressed as
[MATH: \overset{\longleftrightarrow}{PQ}.]

Content:
We use the "[MATH: \longleftrightarrow]" symbol to denote that the line extends forever in both directions.

Content:
Lines can also be indicated with lowercase letters. For example:
